quiz.title: T3.4: Schema Evolution
quiz.description: Test your knowledge of adding indexes to existing properties, %BuildIndices, renaming properties with data, changing datatypes, purging cached queries, and storage definition management.

options: The index definition has a syntax error
The index was compiled but not populated with existing data; %BuildIndices must be run
Standard indexes cannot be used on %String properties
The SQL query has incorrect syntax for using the index
questions.explanation: Compiling a class with a new index only creates the index definition and generates maintenance code for future inserts/updates. The 500,000 existing rows are NOT automatically indexed. The optimizer selects the new (empty) index, which returns no data — making it appear as if no matching rows exist. Running ##class(Sample.Order).%BuildIndices($LB("StatusIdx")) populates the index with existing data. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_defpersobj#GOBJ_indices_build)

questions.question: A developer needs to build only the StatusIdx index on a large table without affecting other indexes. Which code is correct?
options: do ##class(Sample.Order).%BuildIndices()
do ##class(Sample.Order).%BuildIndices($LB("StatusIdx"))
do $SYSTEM.SQL.BuildIndex("Sample.Order", "StatusIdx")
do ##class(Sample.Order).%PurgeIndices($LB("StatusIdx"))
questions.explanation: %BuildIndices accepts a $ListBuild of specific index names to build. Passing $LB("StatusIdx") builds only that index, leaving other indexes untouched. Option A (no args) rebuilds ALL indexes. Option C is not a valid method. Option D purges rather than builds. Selective building is important for large tables where rebuilding all indexes would be time-consuming. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_defpersobj#GOBJ_indices_build)

options: The original Name value is returned because the compiler auto-migrates
An empty string (NULL) because FullName maps to a new empty storage slot
A compilation error because the property cannot be renamed
The original Name value is returned because the storage slot number is preserved
questions.explanation: When a property is renamed, the compiler treats FullName as a new property and assigns it a new slot in the storage definition. The original data remains in the old slot mapped to 'Name'. The result is that FullName appears empty for all existing rows. To fix this, manually edit the storage definition XML to map FullName to the original slot number, or migrate the data. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_storage)

questions.question:
A developer renamed a property from Name to FullName in a persistent class with 100,000 rows. After compiling, FullName returns empty for all existing rows. The developer examines the storage definition and sees:

<Data name="PersonDefaultData">
  <Value name="1"><Value>%%CLASSNAME</Value></Value>
  <Value name="2"><Value>Name</Value></Value>
  <Value name="3"><Value>DOB</Value></Value>
  <Value name="4"><Value>FullName</Value></Value>
</Data>

What should the developer do to make existing data accessible through the FullName property?
options: Run %BuildIndices() to rebuild the data
Change <Value name="2"><Value>Name</Value></Value> to <Value name="2"><Value>FullName</Value></Value> and remove slot 4
Delete all data and reimport it
Run $SYSTEM.SQL.Schema.ImportDDL() to refresh the schema
questions.explanation: The fix is to edit the storage definition to map FullName to slot 2 (where the original Name data resides) and remove the unused slot 4. This tells the runtime to read FullName from the same global position where Name data was stored. After the edit, recompile the class. No data migration is needed because the global data is unchanged. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_storage)

options: The global data is automatically converted to integer format
The global data is unchanged; the old string values remain as-is in the storage slots
The non-numeric values are deleted from the global
The class fails to compile because existing data does not match the new type
questions.explanation: Changing a property's datatype and recompiling does NOT modify the underlying global data. The string values ("85", "N/A", etc.) remain exactly as stored. This creates a risk: non-numeric values like "N/A" are still in the global but may cause unpredictable behavior when accessed through the %Integer property — the result depends on the access path, validation settings, and IRIS version. This is why datatype narrowing on existing data requires a data migration step. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_storage)

options: "000-000-0000" because the InitialExpression is applied retroactively
NULL (empty string) because existing global data has no value for the new slot
An <UNDEFINED> error when accessed
"000-000-0000" because IRIS runs a background migration on compile
questions.explanation: InitialExpression is only applied when a NEW object is created with %New(). Existing rows in the global have no data in the storage slot for Phone, so it reads as empty string (NULL in SQL). The class compilation does NOT modify existing global data. To set default values for existing rows, run an UPDATE statement or ObjectScript loop. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_storage)

questions.question:
A developer adds a bitmap index to an existing class, compiles, and builds it:

Index StatusIdx On Status [Type = bitmap];

A query using the bitmap index works correctly:

&sql(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Sample.Order WHERE Status = 'Pending')

Later, the developer changes the index to a standard index:

Index StatusIdx On Status;

After recompiling (but NOT rebuilding), what happens to queries using StatusIdx?
options: Queries work correctly because the data format is the same
Queries may return incorrect results because the bitmap index data format is different from standard index format
An error occurs because the index type cannot be changed
The index is automatically rebuilt when the type changes
questions.explanation: Bitmap indexes and standard indexes have fundamentally different data structures in the global. Bitmap indexes store bit-string representations; standard indexes store individual key-value entries. After changing the type without rebuilding, the old bitmap data remains in the global but is interpreted as standard index data, leading to incorrect results. Always run %BuildIndices after changing an index type. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_defpersobj#GOBJ_indices_build)

questions.question:
A developer uses CREATE INDEX via SQL DDL:

&sql(CREATE INDEX CityIdx ON TABLE Sample.Person (City))
write SQLCODE

How does this differ from adding the index in the class definition?
options: CREATE INDEX only creates the definition; %BuildIndices must still be called
CREATE INDEX creates the definition AND automatically builds the index for existing data
CREATE INDEX is slower because it does not use the class compiler
CREATE INDEX cannot create bitmap indexes
questions.explanation: The CREATE INDEX DDL statement both creates the index definition in the class and automatically populates it with existing data in one step. This is different from adding an index in the class definition and compiling, where you must separately call %BuildIndices(). CREATE INDEX is convenient for production schema changes because it handles both steps atomically. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RSQL_createindex)

questions.question: A developer modifies a persistent class by adding a column and recompiles. They then notice that some dynamic SQL queries return stale results. What should they do?
options: Restart the IRIS instance to clear all caches
Purge cached queries using $SYSTEM.SQL.Purge() or the Management Portal
Recompile all classes in the namespace
Delete and recreate the %SQL.Statement objects
questions.explanation: When a table structure changes, cached query plans may become stale. While IRIS automatically purges many affected cached queries on schema change, some edge cases (especially with dynamic SQL) may require manual purging. $SYSTEM.SQL.Purge() forces all cached queries in the namespace to be regenerated on next execution. The Management Portal also provides a UI for this. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSQL_queries#GSQL_cachedqueries_purge)

options: The Price data is automatically deleted from the global
Cost is assigned a new slot; the old Price slot remains in the storage definition mapped to the removed property, and the Price data stays in the global
An error prevents compilation when a property is removed
Cost is assigned to the same slot as Price, causing Cost to read old Price values
questions.explanation: The IRIS compiler preserves existing storage slots by default. When Price is removed and Cost is added, the old Price slot remains occupied in the storage definition (still mapped to 'Price'), and Cost is assigned a new slot. The old Price data stays in the global — it is never deleted by schema changes. Cost reads from its new (empty) slot for existing rows. The orphaned Price data wastes storage space but does not cause data corruption. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_storage)

questions.question: A developer needs to rebuild indexes on a 10-million-row table on a live production system. Which approach does InterSystems recommend?
options: do ##class(Sample.BigTable).%BuildIndices()
BUILD INDEX FOR TABLE Sample.BigTable
do ##class(Sample.BigTable).%PurgeIndices() followed by %BuildIndices()
DROP INDEX and CREATE INDEX for each index
questions.explanation: InterSystems recommends using the BUILD INDEX SQL command for live systems. BUILD INDEX acquires an extent lock by default, temporarily marks the index as not selectable (so queries don't use it while it's being built), and any INSERT/UPDATE operations that occur during the build are included in the process. This makes it safe to use on an active system. %BuildIndices() is also available but BUILD INDEX is the preferred approach per the documentation. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSQL_tables#GSQL_indices_building)

options: Queries work correctly because collation only affects display
Queries may return incorrect or incomplete results because the index entries use the old collation
The compilation fails because collation changes require dropping the index first
IRIS automatically rebuilds the index when collation changes
questions.explanation: Index entries are stored using the collation in effect at build time. Changing from EXACT to SQLUPPER means the index should store uppercased values, but existing entries still have the original EXACT values (mixed case). This mismatch causes queries to miss rows or return incorrect results. The index must be rebuilt after any collation change: do ##class(Sample.Class).%BuildIndices($LB("NameIdx")). (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_defpersobj#GOBJ_indices_build)

questions.question: A developer runs TUNE TABLE on a frequently queried table. What happens to existing cached queries for that table?
options: Cached queries are unaffected; the developer must manually purge them
TUNE TABLE automatically recompiles all cached queries for the table so they use the new statistics
Cached queries are deleted and must be re-created manually
TUNE TABLE only affects new queries; existing cached queries keep the old plan until the IRIS instance is restarted
questions.explanation: TUNE TABLE automatically recompiles all existing cached queries for the specified table to use the new statistics values. No manual purge is needed. However, if TUNE TABLE does not change any values (e.g., the data hasn't changed since the last run), cached queries are not recompiled since recompilation would produce the same plans. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RSQL_tunetable)

options: Phone data is unchanged and accessible because it keeps slot 4
Phone may be reassigned to slot 3 and read the old Email data instead
Phone data is automatically migrated from slot 4 to slot 3
The compilation fails because Email data still exists in the global
questions.explanation: When a property is removed, InterSystems IRIS preserves the existing storage definition slots by default. The compiler typically keeps Phone in slot 4 and marks slot 3 (formerly Email) as unused in the storage definition. However, if the developer manually edits or regenerates the storage definition, Phone could be reassigned. Always verify the storage XML after removing properties. The old Email data remains in slot 3 of the global, orphaned but not deleted. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_storage)

options: Run %BuildIndices($LB("CityIdx")) to populate the new bitmap index
Review and fix the storage definition to map Address to the original Addr storage slot
Run a data migration to convert non-numeric Score values before they cause silent data corruption
Purge cached queries so new plans reflect the schema changes
Restart the IRIS instance
questions.explanation: All four steps are needed: (A) New indexes must be built for existing data. (B) Renamed properties need storage definition fixes to read from the original slot. (C) Changing %String to %Integer means non-numeric strings like "N/A" will silently become 0. (D) Cached queries may use stale plans. Restarting IRIS (E) is not required for any of these changes. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_storage)

questions.question: A developer adds a new index to a production table and runs BUILD INDEX to populate it. TUNE TABLE is also run and confirms updated statistics. However, a critical query that should benefit from the new index still uses the old query plan. What is the most likely cause?
options: BUILD INDEX did not complete successfully
The query has a frozen plan that prevents it from being reoptimized
TUNE TABLE must be run a second time for the new index to be recognized
The IRIS instance must be restarted for new indexes to become visible to the optimizer
questions.explanation: Frozen plans are retained across compiles, TUNE TABLE, and even system upgrades. A frozen plan will not be recompiled to use the new index. The developer must explicitly unfreeze the plan (using UNFREEZE PLANS or $SYSTEM.SQL.Statement.UnfreezeStatement()) so a new plan can be generated. The %NOFPLAN keyword can also be used to temporarily ignore the frozen plan for testing. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSQL_queries#GSQL_cachedqueries_freeze)

questions.question: A DBA wants to protect all query plans for a critical table before a system upgrade, so that query performance is not affected. Which approach is correct?
options: FREEZE PLANS FOR TABLE Sample.CriticalTable
PURGE CACHED QUERIES FOR TABLE Sample.CriticalTable
Export the table data before upgrading
Set the table to read-only mode during the upgrade
questions.explanation: FREEZE PLANS FOR TABLE freezes all query plans associated with the specified table. Frozen plans are retained across system upgrades, ensuring query performance is predictable. After the upgrade, the DBA can use the pessimistic strategy: test queries with %NOFPLAN to compare the new plan against the frozen plan, and unfreeze only if the new plan performs better. Plans can also be frozen/unfrozen per-statement, per-schema, or namespace-wide. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSQL_queries#GSQL_cachedqueries_freeze)
